sources: Kenya Ministry of Health - Kenya Health Information System (KHIS) outpatient morbidity summaries

conditions.name: Malaria
conditions.description: Plasmodium infection transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes. Endemic in western Kenya and the coast; a febrile illness in Kenya is treated as suspected malaria until a test says otherwise.
conditions.typical_age_group: All ages; children under 5 and pregnant women at highest risk
conditions.treatment_location: clinic; hospital if any red flag is present
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund)
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for routine diagnosis and treatment; SHIF if admitted; ECCIF if critical care needed
self_care: Take paracetamol for fever and pain

conditions.name: Respiratory Infection
conditions.description: Upper and lower respiratory tract infection ranging from the common cold to pneumonia; a cough lasting more than two weeks must be screened for tuberculosis.
conditions.typical_age_group: All ages; children and the elderly more severe
red_flag_indicators: Cough lasting more than 14 days (tuberculosis screening)
Unable to speak in full sentences
conditions.treatment_location: home if mild; clinic if fever or breathlessness; hospital if severe
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund)
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for consultation, tests and antibiotics; SHIF if admitted with pneumonia
self_care: Honey and ginger for the cough
danger_signs_watch: Cough lasting more than two weeks

conditions.name: Hypertension
conditions.description: Chronically elevated blood pressure. Usually asymptomatic, which is why routine monitoring is the mainstay of control.
red_flag_indicators: Sudden weakness on one side of the body
conditions.treatment_location: clinic for routine monitoring; hospital if a red flag is present
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund)
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for routine monitoring and medicines; ECCIF for hypertensive emergency with organ damage
self_care: Take medicines every day as prescribed
danger_signs_watch: Weakness on one side of the body

conditions.name: Diarrhoea and Gastroenteritis
conditions.description: Intestinal infection causing loose stools. Deaths are caused by dehydration, not by the infection itself, so rehydration is the priority.
conditions.typical_age_group: All ages; children under 5 at highest risk
red_flag_indicators: Sunken eyes or dry mouth (severe dehydration)
No urine passed for many hours
Persistent vomiting - cannot keep fluids down
conditions.treatment_location: home with oral rehydration; clinic if dehydrated; hospital if severe
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund)
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for oral rehydration salts and consultation; SHIF if admitted for intravenous fluids
self_care: Oral rehydration solution after every loose stool
danger_signs_watch: Child becomes floppy or difficult to wake

conditions.name: Chest Pain
conditions.description: Chest pain or pressure that may be cardiac. In a primary care setting this cannot be excluded without an ECG, so cardiac-sounding chest pain is always an emergency.
conditions.typical_age_group: Adults; risk rises with age, diabetes, hypertension and smoking
symptoms: Pain spreading to arm, neck or jaw
red_flag_indicators: Chest pain with shortness of breath
Chest pain spreading to arm, neck or jaw
Chest pain at rest or lasting more than 15 minutes
conditions.treatment_location: HOSPITAL IMMEDIATELY - do not treat at primary level
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 to patient under SHA; ECCIF covers emergency and critical care
conditions.sha_fund: ECCIF (Emergency, Chronic and Critical Illness Fund)
self_care: Stop all activity and sit down
Chew 325 mg aspirin if available and not allergic

conditions.name: Depression and Anxiety
conditions.description: Common mental disorders affecting mood, sleep and function. Under SHA, mental health services are covered without needing a referral, so patients can be directed to care directly.
red_flag_indicators: A plan or means to harm self
Psychosis - hearing voices or fixed false beliefs
Unable to care for self or dependants
conditions.treatment_location: clinic or mental health service; emergency care if suicidal
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund); no referral needed for mental health under SHA
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for primary mental health care and counselling; SHIF for specialist psychiatric care
danger_signs_watch: Not eating or sleeping at all

conditions.name: Urinary Tract Infection
conditions.description: Infection of the bladder or urethra, common in women. Fever with back pain suggests kidney involvement and needs same-day care.
conditions.typical_age_group: More common in adult women; also children and men
symptoms: Burning or pain when passing urine
red_flag_indicators: Fever with back or flank pain (kidney involvement)
conditions.treatment_location: clinic - usually needs antibiotics; hospital if kidney involvement
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund)
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for urine test, consultation and antibiotics; SHIF if admitted with pyelonephritis
self_care: Complete the full course of antibiotics

conditions.name: Skin Infection
conditions.description: Bacterial or fungal skin infection. The key question is whether it is localised or spreading, because spreading infection needs systemic antibiotics.
red_flag_indicators: Red streaks spreading up the limb
Severe pain out of proportion to the wound
Infection on the face or around the eye
conditions.treatment_location: home for small localised infection; clinic if it needs antibiotics
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund)
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for consultation, wound care and antibiotics
self_care: Keep the area clean and dry
Wash hands after touching the area
danger_signs_watch: Red streaks going up the limb

conditions.name: Diabetes Mellitus
conditions.description: Chronic disorder of blood glucose control. Routine monitoring prevents complications; very high or very low glucose is an emergency.
conditions.typical_age_group: Adults; increasingly diagnosed in younger adults
conditions.treatment_location: clinic for routine monitoring; hospital if any red flag is present
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund)
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for routine monitoring and medicines; ECCIF for diabetic emergencies and advanced complications
self_care: Take medicines or insulin as prescribed
Eat regular meals, low in sugar
danger_signs_watch: A foot wound that will not heal

conditions.name: Minor Injury and Trauma
conditions.description: Cuts, bruises and minor wounds. Most are managed locally; the priorities are stopping bleeding, cleaning the wound and tetanus prevention.
conditions.typical_age_group: All ages; young adults most often
symptoms: A wound that may contain a foreign object
red_flag_indicators: Bleeding that will not stop with pressure
A wound from a dirty or rusty object (tetanus risk)
Signs of a broken bone - deformity, inability to move the limb
Numbness or weakness below the injury
Wound to the head, chest, abdomen or eye
conditions.treatment_location: home for minor wounds; clinic for cleaning, stitches or tetanus vaccine; hospital if severe
conditions.estimated_cost_kes: 0 at dispensary or health centre (SHA Primary Healthcare Fund)
conditions.sha_fund: PHF for wound care, suturing and tetanus vaccine; ECCIF for major trauma
self_care: Apply firm pressure to stop bleeding
Clean with clean running water and soap
Elevate the injured part if swollen
danger_signs_watch: Numbness or weakness below the injury
